# Glass types

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools refs render` from research/references/glass-types.yaml. Do not edit. -->

The breakable-glass types: `CfgSetGlassProperties(type, windowLink, alarm, sprite, brokenSprite)`
configures each in `config_preload2.lua`, and a level script places panes with
`SpawnBreakableGlass(type, corner, cornerU, cornerV, uv0, uv1, 0, triangle1, triangle2)`
([World objects: glass](../research/objects.md#glass)).

!!! info "What is complete"

    All 19 types are listed with every argument. Any hit breaks a pane (no hitpoints); what breaking
    does is on [World objects: a pane's life](../research/objects.md#pane). The sprite words' rectangles
    are in the glass pane's sprite batch, whose sheet is not traced.

19 entries. Data: `research/references/glass-types.yaml`.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Hand-written | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | int | | Glass type: `SpawnBreakableGlass`'s first argument and `CfgSetGlassProperties`'. |
| `window_link` | bool | | Second argument (`+0x14`): the pane sits on a navigation jump link, closed while it is whole and opened when it breaks (inferred). |
| `alarm` | bool | | Third argument (`+0x18`): breaking the pane reports a [break-in](crime-types.md#crime-1). |
| `sprite` | hex | | Fourth argument (`+0x1c`): the whole pane's sprite word; its low 16 bits are the rectangle drawn. |
| `broken_sprite` | hex | | Fifth argument (`+0x20`): the sprite word left after the pane breaks (0 draws nothing). |
| `behaviour` | str | yes | What the code does differently for this type. |
| `panes` | int | | `SpawnBreakableGlass` calls that pass the type. |
| `scripts` | list | | The scripts that place panes of it (at most six). |
| `source` | str | yes | Where the entry comes from: a script and binding, an address, a chunk. |
| `evidence` | str | yes | How we know: confirmed-code, confirmed-runtime, inferred or speculative ([evidence levels](../guides/research-workflow.md#evidence-levels)). |
